text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the triggers you described—specifically the stridor worsening with neck flexion and the vomiting episodes—I am highly suspicious of a vascular compression issue. REQUEST TEST: Carotid_Jugular_Ultrasound. Are there any other associated symptoms like a visible mass on the neck or a "pulsatile" quality to the swelling?

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pulmonary Artery Sliding (Aberrant course of the left pulmonary artery). The classic triad of stridor worsening with neck flexion, crying, and feeding, combined with post-prandial vomiting, is highly specific for vascular compression of the trachea by the left pulmonary artery.
